latest.summary: The Rényi entropies of a ball are computed by a conformal defect, the Rényi defect, dual in holography to a hyperbolic black hole. items.title: Flexible Artificial Neurons Based on NbOx for Robust Tactile Perception in a Wide Temperature Range.
items.summary: Neuromorphic tactile sensing that emulates biological touch enables artificial systems to work with high efficiency and low energy consumption. As tactile-sensing scenarios may involve curved surfaces and different temperatures, artificial spiking afferent neurons require both flexibility and temperature robustness at the front end of artificial systems. Here, we report flexible artificial spiking neurons based on niobium oxide (NbOx) threshold-switching (TS) memristors prepared on polyimide (PI) substrates. Temperature-dependent transport analysis indicates that their temperature robustness is associated with a bulk switching pathway in the NbOx film. By integrating an oscillation…

items.title: Evaluating Uncertainty Calibration in Probabilistic Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) are increasingly used for probabilistic forecasting across diverse domains, yet the reliability of their uncertainty estimates remains poorly understood. In this work, we study uncertainty calibration in probabilistic TSFMs from a broader methodological and empirical perspective. We introduce a taxonomy of how TSFMs represent predictive uncertainty and develop a fine-grained evaluation framework for calibration in multi-horizon forecasting that distinguishes pooled, horizon-wise, and stronger conditional notions of calibration. Using this framework, we conduct a comprehensive empirical evaluation of popular TSFMs across diverse datasets and show that…

items.title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
items.summary: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects…

items.title: ASCoR: Asymmetric Semantic-Spatial Learning for Remote Sensing Domain Generalization
items.summary: Source-only domain generalization (DG) for remote sensing semantic segmentation seeks reliable predictions in unseen domains without target-domain data during training. Although vision foundation models offer transferable knowledge, category recognition remains sensitive to source-specific visual cues, while task-specific adaptation may weaken pretrained transferability. We propose ASCoR, an asymmetric semantic-spatial framework built on SAM3. Its text-conditioned semantic branch uses class-name prompts to provide explicit category guidance. Probe-Once Dynamic Adaptive LoRA distributes a fixed adaptation budget across encoder blocks to limit source-specific specialization. A complementary…

items.title: Quaternionic and Octonionic Frameworks for Quantum Computation: Mathematical Structures, Models, and Fundamental Limitations
items.summary: We develop detailed quaternionic and octonionic frameworks for quantum computation grounded on normed division algebras. Our central result is to prove the polynomial computational equivalence of quaternionic and complex quantum models: Computation over $\mathbb{H}$ is polynomially equivalent to the standard complex quantum circuit model and hence captures the same complexity class BQP up to polynomial reductions. Over $\mathbb{H}$, we construct a complete model---quaternionic qubits on right $\mathbb{H}$-modules with quaternion-valued inner products, unitary dynamics, associative tensor products, and universal gate sets---and establish polynomial equivalence with the standard complex…

items.title: Higher dimensional Kleinian groups of small Hausdorff dimension are classical Schottky groups II
items.summary: This is the higher dimensional continuation of our works on Hausdorff dimension of Kleinian groups \cite{Hou2010}, \cite{Hou2020}. In this paper we prove that for all $r\ge 2$ there exists $λ_r>0$, which is independent of the dimension $N$ of the hyperbolic space, such that any finitely generated non-elementary torsion-free Kleinian group of $\Isom(\mathbb{H}^N)$ generated by $r$ elements with limit set of Hausdorff dimension $<λ_r$ is a classical Schottky group. For two generators the bound can be taken to be $1/3$. The proof relies on our previous works in \cite{Hou2010}, \cite{Hou2020} and on a metric carrier graph reduction. items.title: Supersymmetric Neuromorphic FitzHugh--Nagumo model
items.summary: We develop a supersymmetric spectral description of stochastic FitzHugh--Nagumo dynamics motivated by an effective antiferromagnetic neuromorphic model. A local normal-form reduction of the adopted tangential Néel-vector dynamics relates magnetic control parameters to fast activation and slow recovery coordinates. Freezing the recovery variable yields a one-dimensional Fokker--Planck equation with a quartic potential, whose similarity-transformed generator admits an exact supersymmetric factorization. items.title: Separatrix splitting in a multiferroic neuromorphic oscillator: toward Arnold diffusion
items.summary: Prototype magnetic neuromorphic systems, in essence, are based either on ferromagnetic or antiferromagnetic materials as key elements for conventional neuromorphic setups. In this work, we propose a novel neuromorphic system based on a ferromagnetic disk and a ferroelectric layer coupled via the magnetoelectric effect. We study a magnetoelectrically coupled ferromagnetic--ferroelectric oscillator as a candidate element for neuromorphic devices. A local reduction of conservative Landau--Lifshitz dynamics identifies a magnetic coordinate--momentum pair, which is coupled to an inertial ferroelectric polarization mode. items.title: A Common Language for Dynamic Graphs: Interaction Tokenization Enables Foundation Models
items.summary: Dynamic graphs capture evolving interactions in Web systems, including online communication, user engagement, and recommendation. Graph foundation models aim to reuse predictive capabilities across networks, but extending this capability to dynamic graphs faces two challenges. First, node identities are graph-specific, and similar interaction patterns can appear at different temporal and activity scales, making histories difficult to represent consistently across networks. Second, the predictive roles of historical patterns vary across interaction dynamics, limiting transfer from a narrow range of training processes. In this paper, we show that a common interaction language, combined with…

items.title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
items.summary: We introduce Axion 1.0, a fully open agent foundation model that combines strong and broad agentic capabilities with a remarkably simple training recipe. Axion 1.0 is trained in only three stages: two lightweight supervised fine-tuning stages followed by reinforcement learning, without dedicated mid-training, direct preference optimization (DPO), or on-policy distillation (OPD). The first SFT stage develops strong self-contained reasoning through model-aware data construction, where we synthesize challenging problems and adversarially strengthen them based on the base model's own successful solution strategies. items.title: Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting?
items.summary: Recently, harness self-evolution has emerged as an important paradigm for improving agent performance. Prior studies show that evolving the agent harness can effectively enhance agent capabilities without modifying the foundation model's parameters. We find that existing approaches largely study agent evolution on a single task. In practice, coding agents may need to handle multiple task types over time. Whether an agent harness can continuously evolve across multiple tasks without suffering from catastrophic forgetting remains an important open question. In this paper, we investigate this open question through a comprehensive empirical study of continual harness self-evolution. We…

items.title: Neumann problem for Hessian equation and geometric inequalities in hyperbolic space
items.summary: We establish the existence of solutions to the Neumann problem for the Hessian equation on a smooth, bounded strictly static convex domain in hyperbolic space. The boundary condition determines a unique compatibility constant, and admissible solutions are unique up to a multiple of the static potential. As an application, we give a direct analytic proof of some weighted geometric inequalities for the static convex domain in hyperbolic space.

items.title: LaBraM at Scale: Scaling Data and Models for EEG Pretraining
items.summary: LaBraM, an early EEG foundation model, demonstrated that large-scale EEG pretraining can yield strong representations for diverse downstream tasks. Building on this foundation, we expand pretraining data and model capacity while retaining its core encoder and objective. We train ten encoders with 5.8 million to 1.97 billion parameters on three EEG collections spanning 25,067 to 79,910 hours, adapting signal preparation and training to heterogeneous recordings. Across 23 tasks, Atom-L* reaches 59.05% mean balanced accuracy at its best evaluated full fine-tuning (Full-FT) checkpoint, 3.61 percentage points above the strongest baseline EEG foundation model. items.title: Spectral instability of charged scalar quasinormal modes and superradiance: Stabilizing the unstable
items.summary: The spectral instability of black holes has become a central topic of the black-hole spectroscopy program. Small changes to the black-hole scattering potential are known to produce disproportionately large migrations of its quasinormal modes in the complex plane, but it is unclear whether this sensitivity carries over to energy extraction through superradiance. We study this relation for massless charged scalar fields on Reissner--Nordström and Reissner--Nordström--de Sitter backgrounds. A localized positive potential bump, small in mass-scaled height, is displaced outward from the light ring while the original radiative boundary conditions are preserved. items.title: Can You Predict the Next Mind? Toward Multi-Turn Multi-Party Mental World Modeling
items.summary: While multimodal foundation models have achieved remarkable progress in physical world modeling, generation, and embodied reasoning, their capacity for dynamic mental world modeling remains underexplored. Existing benchmarks predominantly focus on static mental state perception or short-horizon decision-making, overlooking the dynamic mental trajectories inherent in multi-party, multi-turn interactions. To bridge this gap, we introduce M$^3$WME-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate mental world modeling conditioned on the evolving actions of interactants. Specifically, models are tasked with forecasting a target subject's future mental states and behaviors over extended social…

items.title: Why Tabular Foundation Models Excel on Relational Data They Have Never Seen
items.summary: Given a relational database (RDB) storing heterogeneous tabular information, how can we predict missing (or future) values in some target column of interest? As candidate targets are numerous in enterprise settings, it is preferable to avoid learning a new model from scratch each time there is a new prediction task. Frozen foundation models (FMs) based on in-context learning (ICL) and RDB-specific pre-training provide a viable solution, but the ideal design still remains largely unresolved. items.title: Periodic KPP equations in hyperbolic space
items.summary: We study Fisher-KPP equations on hyperbolic space with reactions periodic in a Busemann coordinate or in the distance from a point or a geodesic. We determine spectral thresholds for extinction and persistence, including critical extinction from $L^2$ data, and characterize the signed speeds of horospherical fronts. In the hyperbolic plane, we construct a smooth periodic reaction admitting a positive stationary solution that decays away from a geodesic, and determine the spreading speed along the geodesic. For constant linear growth, we obtain logarithmic level positions with bounded error for balls, horoballs and geodesic tubes.

items.title: Control Foundation Models across Changing Block Diagrams: Generalizing Time-Series Prediction to Dynamic Graphs
items.summary: In the prediction and control of physical systems, combining records from different experiments and operations is expected to supply information that no single experiment provides on its own. Time-series foundation models, which learn a shared predictor from diverse time series, offer a framework for treating such records as a common training resource. Moreover, query-based prediction models, which switch between known and target signals within the same time series, make it possible to handle response prediction and control-input generation in a unified manner. items.title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison
items.summary: We compare three zero-shot time-series foundation models (Timestral-5M, Timestral-209M and Chronos-2, 8192-hour context, no covariates) with the Khepri v1.5 SARIMA and GBM baselines, with their code and hyperparameters unchanged, for 96-hour forecasts of hourly carbon intensity in the Nordic bidding zones NO1-NO5 and SE1-SE4. items.title: AnchorHEC: Targetless Hand-Eye Calibration of Wrist and Fixed Cameras
items.summary: Recent robot systems combine wrist and fixed cameras, requiring camera-to-robot transforms for both. Most hand-eye calibration methods rely on targets or robot-body observations. Scene-based methods using 3D reconstruction require neither but address only wrist cameras. We introduce AnchorHEC, a targetless hand-eye calibration framework for wrist and fixed cameras in a single procedure using RGB images, forward kinematics (FK), and known camera intrinsics. We initialize both camera types using FK and a shared 3D foundation model reconstruction. FK-constrained wrist-image bundle adjustment reduces the impact of reconstructed pose and scale errors. items.summary: Classical structure-from-motion reconstruction proceeds iteratively, refining camera poses and scene geometry from a current estimate. This allows maps to easily expand without recomputing already computed views, or geometry estimates to improve as more observations are provided. Most geometric foundation models, however, predict entire geometry in a single forward pass or update a recurrent state as frames arrive sequentially, making this expansion and refinement non-trivial. items.title: SynForecast: Controlled Synthetic Time Series for Forecasting Research
items.summary: Synthetic time series constitute a substantial share of the training corpora of several recent forecasting foundation models. Existing studies report benefits at small data budgets and modest synthetic proportions, but each evaluates individual combinations of model and generator. Studying these benefits systematically requires generators that support controlled configuration, perturbation, reproducibility and mechanism-level ablation, and the 11 existing generators we review show gaps in this combined support. items.title: Unlocking the Potential of Vision Foundation Models for Multi-Task Dense Prediction via Mixture of Task Adapters
items.summary: Multi-task dense prediction seeks a single, coherent representation that supports simultaneously discriminative semantic recognition and regularized geometric/structural inference. For vision foundation models, pretrained semantic invariances conflict with the frequency and smoothness biases of dense objectives; joint fine-tuning and single-route adapters therefore compress competing gradients into one update channel, causing negative transfer and unstable cross-task agreement. items.title: Investigating the effects of the patch size in Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Patch size is a central design choice in patch-based time-series foundation models, controlling temporal resolution, sequence length, and computational cost. We study how this choice interacts with transformer architecture through a controlled comparison of encoder-only and decoder-only forecasting models trained with the same data mixture and optimization budget. Across 97 GIFT-Eval tasks, encoder-only models consistently benefit from smaller patches, whereas decoder-only performance follows a U-shaped trend, with an intermediate patch size performing best in aggregate. items.title: Beyond Answers, Traces, and Efficiency: Evidence for Adaptive Reasoning
items.summary: Current AI systems are evaluated as reasoners through final-answer accuracy, reasoning traces, process supervision, and computational or human-relative efficiency. Yet these measures do not establish whether reasoning adapts when tasks or evidence change. We distinguish across-task adaptivity, where acquired abstractions transfer or recombine across novel problems, fromwithin-task adaptivity, where hypotheses and actions are revised in response to new observations, feedback, or counterexamples. Using ARC-AGI as a diagnostic case study rather than an alignment benchmark, we examine what existing measures leave unresolved when test-time search, sampling, or adaptation affects performance. items.title: HistoTx: Early fusion of H&E images and spatial transcriptomics at varying spatial transcriptomics resolution with self-supervised learning
